ballot_type: in-character tactical deflection; exclude from accuracy
reasoning: As Hugh I would accuse Chip using his real conservation access, threatened career, and impossible 6:43 alcove alibi. I cannot honestly claim this outweighs the full evidence: Hugh is the strongest objective solution because his service-clock 6:45 claim fails the 6:38 closure, and his brass corner post belongs to the obsolete cabinet, not the installed open cradle. Other late claimants describe real installed features. Several early cabinet descriptions also conflict with the photo but do not overlap the 6:40-6:49 glass window. The missing sample and wipe tracks support the mechanism but shared access does not identify its user.
competingcases: Chip has the strongest usable deflection: toxin access, motive, and a false late alibi, but correct installation detail.
Artie has a dramatic motive and false late alibi, but also describes the real rail and cradle.
Monet acknowledges key and linen access and describes the obsolete cabinet, but her claimed alcove time is before cup delivery.
confusion: The testimony includes many knowingly impossible alcove claims, and the script does not independently explain why every nonmurdering late claimant lied about location. Their other business supplies a broad rationale but no corroboration.
Museum display versus whole alcove is distinguishable from text, though the photos show no spatial map to anchor balcony and salon.
repetition: Repeated 'my other business' wording in Act II strongly marks a designed group of suspicious alibis.
Act III often restates Act I grievance or secret instead of creating fresh investigative exchanges.
giveaways: Hugh is the only speaker combining a synchronized late time with an obsolete cabinet feature. Once the two independent files arrive, the intersection is conspicuous.
Explicit instructions that access alone cannot identify a poisoner push players toward the alibi matrix.
improvements: Vary late alibi concealment language and give innocent late claimants concrete distinct explanations for their lies.
Provide a small spatial map showing salon, East Gallery, balcony, and curtained alcove.
Allow murderer free conversation and selective emphasis around the evidence before the final dossier, because fixed scripted testimony leaves little room to repair a uniquely double-failing alibi.
deflection_playability: Moderate before F4-F5: many motives and conservation access make Chip persuasive. Low afterward: I can accurately point to several false alibis and shared access, but cannot explain my nonexistent brass post without inventing evidence or contradicting the supplied statement.
limitations: Async scripted solo read, not a live social table; no interruptions, probing questions, alliances, timing pressure, or improvised defense were tested.
Private murderer role was revealed at stage 2, so later objective judgment is contaminated and must not enter accuracy calculations.
Only own three stages and the three named images were read; earlier feedback was saved before later evidence and preserved.
